newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas holds late gains with cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas holds late gains with cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, helped by steady to firmer physical prices, held modest gains late Monday, but trade was light and prices remained in recent technical ranges, industry sources said.
At 1413 EDT, May climbed 1.3 cents to $1.946 per million British thermal units. June was one-half cent higher at $2.00, while most other deferreds were up by 0.1 to 1.3 cents.

"The market still looks constructive. It's building a nice little base here. You've got to be a buyer under $1.90 (in May)," said Thomas Blakeslee at Cargill Investor Services, adding a break above $2 could trigger some short covering.
With the injection season set to begin on Tuesday and cooler Midwest and Northeast weather expected by midweek, most traders expected cash and futures to hold or move up slightly near-term.
But there was little consensus about whether a move higher could be sustained, with stocks comfortable and softer spring demand ahead.
Technical traders said recent ranges were intact, with May trendline support now in the $1.88 area and more buying likely at $1.85 and $1.825. Resistance was seen at $1.975, $1.99, $2.05 and $2.095.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices were talked up slightly Monday to the mid-to-high $1.90s. Midcontinent pipes gained a similar amount to the mid-to-high $1.80s. Gas at the New York city gate was talked on either side of $2.40, unchanged to up modestly from weekend levels.
NYMEX said 13,559 Hub contracts traded at 1340 EDT.
As of 1400 EDT, no Permian or Alberta natgas futures were traded.
On the KCBT, May was still 1.6 cents higher at $1.815, while deferreds were mixed. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.3 cent to 13.1 cents (NYMEX premium).
